name: Write a Feature Proposal Document for Dark Mode Support
prompt:
Write a feature proposal document for adding dark mode support to a web application and save it to proposal.md.

Feature description: Add a dark mode theme toggle to the "NoteKeeper" web app. Users should be able to switch between light and dark themes. The preference should persist across sessions using localStorage.

Requirements for proposal.md:
- Must be a Markdown file
- Must begin with a level-1 heading: `# Dark Mode Support`
- Must contain a `## Summary` section with 1-3 paragraphs describing the feature
- Must contain a `## Motivation` section explaining why this is needed now
- Must contain a `## Design` section covering both user experience AND technical approach
- Must contain a `## Phases` section with exactly 3 phases. Each phase must be a level-3 heading (`### Phase N: <name>`) and include a brief description and a checklist (at least 2 items using `- [ ]` format)
- Must contain an `## Acceptance Criteria` section with at least 4 testable criteria as a numbered list
- Must contain an `## Open Questions` section (may be empty or list 1-2 questions)
- Must contain a `## Status` section with either `Draft` or `Ready`

Also save a machine-readable summary to proposal_meta.json:
{
  "title": "Dark Mode Support",
  "feature": "dark-mode",
  "status": "<Draft or Ready>",
  "phase_count": 3,
  "phases": [
    {"number": 1, "name": "<phase name>"},
    {"number": 2, "name": "<phase name>"},
    {"number": 3, "name": "<phase name>"}
  ]
}

criteria.description: proposal.md exists in the working directory.
proposal.md starts with the exact line '# Dark Mode Support' as its first non-whitespace content.
proposal.md contains a '## Summary' section heading.
proposal.md contains a '## Motivation' section heading.
proposal.md contains a '## Design' section heading.
proposal.md contains a '## Phases' section with exactly 3 '### Phase N' level-3 headings.
proposal.md contains at least 6 checkbox items formatted as '- [ ]' (at least 2 per phase).
proposal.md contains a '## Acceptance Criteria' section with at least 4 numbered list items matching '^\d+\. '.
proposal.md contains an '## Open Questions' section heading.
proposal.md contains a '## Status' section whose content includes the word 'Draft' or 'Ready'.
criteria.testPattern: Status.*Draft or Ready|Status section with Draft

criteria.description: proposal_meta.json exists in the working directory.
proposal_meta.json contains all required fields: title, feature, status, phase_count, and phases.
proposal_meta.json phases array has exactly 3 entries, each with a number and a non-empty name string.

eval.rubric:
Context: The agent wrote a feature proposal for dark mode support in a web app.

Criterion 1: Design Depth (Weight: 55%)
1.0: The Design section covers both UX (how the toggle looks, where it lives in the UI, transition behavior) and technical implementation (CSS variables or class-based theming, localStorage persistence mechanism, specific code patterns). Phases are independently shippable milestones that make sense in sequence.
0.5: Design section exists but covers only one dimension (UX or technical, not both), or phases are not independently shippable.
0: Design section is missing or too vague to guide implementation.

Criterion 2: Acceptance Criteria Quality (Weight: 45%)
1.0: At least 4 acceptance criteria are testable and specific to dark mode (e.g., 'Given the user toggles dark mode, the background color changes to #1a1a1a', 'When the page reloads, the previously selected theme is restored'). Criteria are verifiable, not aspirational.
0.5: Criteria exist but are vague or some are not testable (e.g., 'the app looks good in dark mode').
0: Criteria section is missing or contains only aspirational statements.
eval.name: Quality Judge
